treatment: Per-genome differences from the intact assembly (median): fragmentation alone changes coding density by -0.04 points, genome size by 0.000 Mb and GC by 0.00 points, and raises the CDS count by 288 because genes are split at contig ends; fragmentation plus 4.4% deletion changes coding density by -0.04 points and genome size by -0.263 Mb. The FSM-against-RGM differences these must be set against are 2.73 Mb of genome size and 1.0 point of coding density. Gene recovery falls to 95.8% under fragmentation alone and 91.5% with deletion. A family genuinely present would have to be missed in at least 54 of the 59 high-completeness FSM MAGs to be scored lost clade-wide (independent-loss probability 5e-52).

Bakta calls genes with Pyrodigal in closed mode and so loses every gene that runs off a contig end: shredding alone costs a median 3.00 points of Bakta coding density, against 0.04 points for standalone Prodigal, and it reproduces the whole gap seen between the two callers in real assemblies (+2.69 points simulated, +2.44 points observed in the MAGs, against +0.46 in the reference assemblies). Fragmentation adds a median of one Bakta pseudogene. That is a lower bound on the real binning artefact, because shredding reproduces contig breakage but not assembly error; the observed isolate-to-MAG pseudogene offsets are +3 in RGM and +11.5 in SGM. Both run in the direction that would inflate FSM's pseudogene count, which is the lowest in the ingroup.
